Quick reference for using the app, tokens, and remote proxy format.
A simple CONNECT payload usually starts with the target host and keeps the header closed with a blank line.

When the port is empty, http:// uses 80, https:// uses 443, and socks/socks4/socks4a/socks5 uses 1080. Without a scheme, the default is usually 80, or 443 when the payload path uses the SSL/SNI default.
host:port, user:pass@host:port, http://host:port, https://host:port, socks://host:port, socks4://host:port, socks4a://host:port, socks5://host:port, [2001:db8::1]:1080

Token names are case-insensitive. If host, remote proxy, and SNI all use tokens, at least one of them must still contain a literal value. Repeat tokens with *N, e.g. [crlf*2]. The literal escapes \\r and \\n inside the payload also turn into real line breaks. Aliases: [udpcustom] = [udp_custom], [udpcustom_host] = [udp_custom_host], [udpcustom_port] = [udp_custom_port], [slow] = [slowdns], [slow_host] = [slowdns_host], [slow_port] = [slowdns_port], [ws-key] = [ws_key].

[rotate] and [random] split the payload into variants tried in order; [random] also shuffles them. [rotate=a;b;c] cycles through the values in turn; [random=a;b;c] picks one at random. Works for host, remote proxy, SNI, and payload.

Split tokens cut the payload into separate requests. [split], [splitNoDelay], and [instant_split] send the chunks back to back; [delay], [delay_split], and [split_delay] wait 1 second between chunks, with no wait after the last one.

To create a Short URL, HTTP Custom sends the source URL to eprdv.link, which fetches and relays the config content.
